name: Question 1
problem: Find the total area of the region bounded by the graph of the curve $y=3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}$ and the $x$-axis.
worked_solution:
We find the area of the region bounded by the graph of the curve and the $x$-axis by calculating the integral

$$
A={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}.
$$

We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}\,\text{d}x
$$

We start by calculating the first of these integrals:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}3{x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x
$$

We calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let $u={x}^{3}$,  then $\text{d}u=3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x.$ Hence, the antiderivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={e}^{u}+C \\  & ={e}^{{x}^{3}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}3{x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}3{x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{({e}^{{x}^{3}})|}_{a}^{0} \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }({e}^{0}-{e}^{{a}^{3}}) \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand $3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}$ is an **even** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=1.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }3{x}^{2}{e}^{-|x{|}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =1+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We find the area of the region bounded by the graph of the curve and the x-axis by calculating the integral A=∫−∞∞3x2e−|x|3.

We break up the integral as follows: ∫−∞∞3x2e−|x|3dx=∫−∞03x2e−|x|3dx+∫0∞3x2e−|x|3dx

We start by calculating the first of these integrals: ∫−∞03x2e−|x|3dx=∫−∞03x2ex3dx

We calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let u=x3, then du=3x2dx. Hence, the antiderivative is ∫3x2ex3dx=∫eudu=eu+C=ex3+C.

So, we get

∫−∞03x2e−|x|3dx=∫−∞03x2ex3dx=lima→−∞∫a03x2ex3dx=lima→−∞(ex3)|a0=lima→−∞(e0−ea3)=1−0=1.

Now, notice that the integrand 3x2e−|x|3 is an even function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

∫0∞3x2e−|x|3dx=1.

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that ∫−∞∞3x2e−|x|3dx=∫−∞03x2e−|x|3dx+∫0∞3x2e−|x|3dx=1+1=2.
